clue.text: Any of several screen performers using short sawn-off rifle

indicators.note: short says the word for sawn-off loses its final letter

parts.note: something sawn off has been cut
to rifle a place is to sack or plunder it

explanation.surface: A gunman hacks down a rifle barrel to make a crude weapon for the movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the last letter from CUT, leaving CU. The Cusacks are an Irish acting family (Cyril, Sinéad, Niamh), and there is an American one too (John, Joan).
explanation.definitionFit: Several members of the surname's family are well-known film and stage actors, so any of them fits.

clue.text: Affected sense, perhaps, picked up in travellers' area

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A mannered sensibility is detected among people on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch for tents or caravans is the area where travellers stop.

clue.text: Anglicans blocking request to repeat enchanting activity

indicators.note: blocking says the church letters sit in the middle of the request, obstructing it

parts.note: saying sorry? asks someone to repeat what they said
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Churchgoers get in the way of a demand for an encore of a charming performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Witchcraft or magic is the activity of casting spells, enchanting people.

clue.text: Clubs unobjectionable but devoid of attraction

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
something unobjectionable is inoffensive, doing no harm

explanation.surface: The nightclubs are inoffensive but have no appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking charm means having no appeal or allure at all.

clue.text: Explain in detail losing boxer's experience?

definitions.meaning: to set something out clearly, step by step
a knocked-out boxer has a period of being unconscious

explanation.surface: A pundit is asked to describe exactly what happens to the fighter who loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into SPELL (a period) and OUT (unconscious), as a floored boxer is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to state something plainly and fully, leaving nothing unexplained.

clue.text: Lifts in theatre form part of one's job?

definitions.text: Lifts in theatre form part of one's job?

parts.words: Lifts in theatre form part of one's job?
parts.note: lifts are facelifts and theatre is the operating theatre, so this is a cosmetic surgeon

explanation.surface: It sounds like a stagehand whose work includes operating the stage hoists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifts' and 'theatre' suggest the stage, but they are a facelift and the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgeon performs facelifts in the operating theatre as part of the work.

clue.text: Many hungry young men in effect

indicators.note: in effect says the young men are, effectively, holding the nothing inside them

parts.note: lads are young men
someone hungry has nothing inside, and nothing is O

explanation.surface: Plenty of famished youths, effectively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hungry' supplies O as having nothing in the stomach, and 'in effect' puts it inside LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a great quantity or a large number is said to be lots, a heap.

clue.text: Note well row probing excessive consumption? That's agreed

indicators.note: probing says the note and row push inside the overdose

parts.note: OD is an overdose, taking too much of a drug
NB is nota bene, Latin for note well
an oar is used to row; a rower is also an oar

explanation.surface: A warning note about a quarrel over binge drinking, followed by a consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but stands for the oar used in rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on side with a plan, in accord with others, means having agreed to it.

clue.text: Moderate much of painting technique

indicators.note: much of says the word loses a little, its final letter

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk

explanation.surface: A tone down for most of an artist's method.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to tone it down or soften it, as in tempering criticism.

clue.text: Route aged flier devised — it's shared by South Americans?

indicators.note: devised says these letters are worked out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An old pilot plans a route over a place South Americans have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: The archipelago at South America's tip is split between Argentina and Chile.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago at the southern tip of the continent is divided between Chile and Argentina.

clue.text: Damage good porcelain — and feature of Hispanic blind?

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or damage it
Arita is a kind of Japanese porcelain named after its town of origin

explanation.surface: Someone breaks fine china and mentions a Spanish window blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' is not a window covering but British slang for a drinking bout, at which a Mexican cocktail might well feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila cocktail is the kind of drink that would be downed at a Latin American booze-up.

clue.text: Revolver, say, hoarded by criminal bumptiously

indicators.note: hoarded by says the letters are stored away inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gun is stashed by a cocky crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' looks like a gun but is the 1966 Beatles LP; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolver is a Beatles long-player, an example of a collection of recorded songs.

clue.text: Vessel making delivery round back of port

indicators.note: round says the delivery word goes around the next letter

parts.note: in cricket a seamer is a ball that deviates off the seam, a kind of delivery

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of port

explanation.surface: A ship brings a consignment around to the rear of the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like a shipment but is the cricket sense, a bowled ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Like a proper map, characterising mountain for trekkers?

definitions.meaning: a map drawn with consistent proportions to the ground
a mountain is something hikers set out to climb

explanation.surface: Walkers want an accurate chart and a peak to tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes SCALE as the verb to climb: a mountain is there for trekkers to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A properly drawn map keeps every distance in fixed proportion, the cartographer's phrase for which is this one.

clue.text: Source of flavouring in bird, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken and another spelling is entered

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs a chicken with a herb, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like the thing being stuffed, but means a stretch in prison, as in 'doing bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: A culinary herb whose leaves season stews and roasts is a source of flavour.

clue.text: A cold drink disciple drained as appreciative token

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
cola is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: drained empties the word of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A follower empties a cold drink as a gesture of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or tribute given in praise is a token of appreciation.

clue.text: Tale involving female initiate's source of strength

indicators.note: involving says the tale wraps round the female letter

parts.note: a lie is a made-up tale
to blood someone is to initiate them; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A story involving a woman explains what gives a newcomer strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The vital force that keeps something going is its source of strength, like blood to a body.

clue.text: Name advantage in replacement of one container

indicators.note: in replacement of says the advantage stands in for the one

parts.note: to cite is to name or quote
I is the Roman numeral one
an asset is an advantage

explanation.surface: Instructions for swapping out a container to gain an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in replacement of one' swaps I in CITE for ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cassette is a plastic case holding the reel, so it is a kind of container.

clue.text: Investigator among schools heard murmur by lodge

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken aloud and the name is entered

parts.note: a dove's murmur is a coo, and to lodge or stash something is to stow it, placed side by side

explanation.surface: Someone looking into schools overhears whispering beside a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' are not classrooms but schools of fish: Jacques Cousteau was the French underwater explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French oceanographer spent his life studying marine life, schools of fish included.

clue.text: Acceptable rally in action in square?

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's just not on'
a drive is a campaign, as is a rally of support

explanation.surface: An acceptable protest takes place in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the square is the central area of pitches, and an on-drive is a shot played to the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket stroke hit straight to the on side is an action played out on the square.

clue.text: Fine Italian article about a range of animals

indicators.note: about says the fine letter and article together go around the a

parts.note: F is the pencil grading for fine
una is the Italian feminine indefinite article

explanation.surface: A refined Italian piece covers a wide variety of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A between F and UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for the animal life of a region covers the whole range of its creatures.

clue.text: Take advantage of some revolutionary cigarettes I lit up

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a radical's habit of smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: To make use of something for one's own ends is to exploit it, to benefit from it.

clue.text: Blur, first sign of drunkenness in self-complacent European

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the self-satisfied word

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied

indicators.note: first sign of picks the first letter of drunkenness

explanation.surface: A blur, the first symptom of a self-satisfied European getting tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear or smudge makes outlines indistinct, a blur.

clue.text: How one might describe performing jazz player's diaphragm?

definitions.text: How one might describe performing jazz player's diaphragm?

parts.words: How one might describe performing jazz player's diaphragm?
parts.note: the word also names the part of the body containing the diaphragm

explanation.surface: A question about how to describe a jazz musician's breathing muscle during a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: A riff is a repeated jazz phrase, so a player in the act is MID RIFF; read as one word it is the middle of the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The front of the body between chest and waist is the region where the diaphragm lies.

clue.text: Cool rental property in bay

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A trendy holiday rental beside the bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea running inland is a small bay or creek.

clue.text: Special writer with obsession put over doings

indicators.note: put over says the pieces are turned upside down, read backwards in a down light or across

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
a bug is an enthusiasm or craze, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: A dedicated author with a fixation transfers it onto some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doings' is British slang for odds and ends whose names escape you, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for bits and bobs, miscellaneous items or contraptions.

clue.text: What squaddies do is broadcast in row

definitions.meaning: squaddies (British slang for private soldiers) practise marching and parade-ground exercises
to sow seed in a straight furrow rather than scattering it

explanation.surface: Soldiers' activities are shown on air during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is not the radio sense but sowing seed; a drill is a row of sown seed or the machine sowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers practise drill on parade, and a drill is also a planted row of seeds.

clue.text: Smith, maybe, over in city with a clear view?

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a clear view has no mist

explanation.surface: A blacksmith stands above the town, enjoying the clear weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations, is the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Smith was the founding figure of modern political economy, an example of an expert on markets.

clue.text: Seat can be obtained by this horse bucking head

definitions.text: Seat can be obtained by this

indicators.note: bucking head is read as shrugging off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a selection is a horse picked to bet on

explanation.surface: A rider stays in the saddle on a horse that keeps throwing its head about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a saddle but is a parliamentary seat; 'bucking' is read as throwing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate wins a parliamentary seat by being voted in at the polls.

clue.text: Keep constant summary of billboard?

definitions.meaning: to stay faithful to or stick to something
a hoarding's message in short is that it has an advertisement in this spot

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to the short message on a poster site.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it 2,4 as AD HERE: what a billboard sums up by its very presence.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to a rule or belief is to remain faithful to it, keeping it steadily.
